## Ideal gas conversion (`ideal-gas`) {#sec-ch02-ideal-gas}

### Summary

The ideal gas maps total energy to pressure after subtracting kinetic energy with the metric contraction. Floors can prevent the reverse map from being an exact inverse. The factory alias is `ideal-gas`.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** The ideal-gas conversion between conserved and primitive states: pressure from the total energy minus the kinetic energy with the metric contraction (@eq-ch02-ideal-gas-pressure).

**Data.** In: the conserved cell averages `hydro_u`, $\rho$ [kg m$^{-3}$], $m_a$ [kg m$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$], $E$ [J m$^{-3}$] (total mass, no species rows), or the primitive `hydro_w`, $\rho$, $\mathbf v$ [m s$^{-1}$], $p$ [Pa]. Out: the other representation in the same rows, $T$ [K] and $c_s$ [m s$^{-1}$]; constant heat capacity and no reference-energy offset.

**Placement.** At every conserved-to-primitive and primitive-to-conserved conversion of the step.

**Activation.** `type: ideal-gas`; the default EOS stays `moist-mixture`.

**Guarantee / limits.** The cell-local algebra is exact before the floors; a floor can make the reverse map inexact.

**Evidence.** `test_eos.release` asserts the zero internal-energy offset ($10^{-12}$ absolute and relative, prescribed by `allclose`); no run of these ctest entries is recorded for this chapter at the pin (missing evidence). `ideal-gas_check.py` is report-only, run with its committed output `src/snapy_report/ch02/ideal-gas_check.out`.
:::

### Derivation

For a calorically perfect gas, $e=c_{v,\mathrm d}T$ and $p=\rho R_{\mathrm d}T$,
where $T$ is in $\mathrm K$ and the heat capacities and $R_{\mathrm d}$ are in
$\mathrm{J\,kg^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$. Eliminating $T$ with
$R_{\mathrm d}=(\gamma_{\mathrm d}-1)c_{v,\mathrm d}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
\rho e&=E-\tfrac12\sum_{a=1}^3v^a m_a,\\
p&=(\gamma_{\mathrm d}-1)\rho e,\\
T&=p/(\rho R_{\mathrm d}),\\
c_s^2&=\gamma_{\mathrm d}p/\rho.
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch02-ideal-gas-pressure}

@eq-ch02-ideal-gas-pressure is implemented by `_prim2cons` in {{< code src/eos/ideal_gas.cpp IdealGasImpl::_prim2cons >}}.

The kinetic contraction pairs contravariant velocity with covariant momentum, so a coordinate raise is required
before computing it from conserved data. Integrating a uniform thermodynamic state over a cell multiplies both
mass and energy by its volume; division by the volume returns these same relations. Applied to nonuniform cell
averages, this is a closure on the average state, not an exact average of a nonlinear pointwise EOS.
`ideal-gas_check.py` verifies the inverse maps with a nonorthogonal positive metric.

### Numerical method

`_prim2cons` applies primitive floors, multiplies velocities by density, lowers momentum and adds kinetic energy,
then applies the conserved limiter (`apply_conserved_limiter_`) in {{< code src/eos/ideal_gas.cpp IdealGasImpl::_prim2cons >}}.
`_cons2prim` applies conserved floors, dispatches the fused conversion, then applies primitive floors.
The operation is local to each supplied cell, with no special wall, seam or RK-stage stencil.
